results.content:
## Introducing Firefox Enterprise

Firefox Enterprise is built for organizations with strict security, governance, and compliance requirements. It pairs the Firefox browser, built on Mozilla’s independent Gecko engine, with a management console organizations can run on their own infrastructure. From that console, IT teams can centrally manage browser policy and access, govern how data moves through the browser and set controls around AI use.

IT and security teams get more control over their data, IT infrastructure and browser environment — helping strengthen technological independence and operational resilience. [...] That means putting institutions in real control of the infrastructure and data they depend on, without asking them to rebuild or start over. Closing blind spots. Defining where policies, access and data live. Keeping core management within the institution’s environment. And bringing an overlooked layer — the browser — under institutional control.

Firefox Enterprise is unveiling across Europe with an initial sales focus on France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with more markets to follow. Thunderbird Enterprise is also in development, extending this customer-controlled approach to email and communications. We’ll have more to share as that work progresses.

If your organization wants greater control over its browser infrastructure, we’d like to work with you. [...] Finally, Firefox Enterprise is built to live alongside the systems that IT operations already use. Keep your identity provider. Keep your SIEM. Keep your MDM. Just add a browser whose management infrastructure you operate, so you decide where data lives and have greater visibility into how it moves.

For us, supporting the goal of technological sovereignty comes down to four things: More control. More transparency. More choice. More resilience.

Learn more about Firefox Enterprise.

## A big bet on familiar ground

# With an Eye on Europe, Mozilla Launches Firefox Enterprise With Self-Hosted Browser Management

Mozilla has announced Firefox Enterprise, a commercial offering for businesses and government agencies. It combines Firefox with a management console that organizations can run on their own servers.

 Abhishek Prakash

Abhishek Prakash

3 min read

Warp Terminal

Mozilla has a new product called Firefox Enterprise. Which is basically Firefox but built around the needs of private and government organizations.

The idea is simple. If staff uses a browser for work, organizations should be able to control its settings, protect company data, and decide where its management system runs. [...] ## A good fit for Europe's push for digital independence

Mozilla's initial sales focus is France, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, with more markets planned. Its announcement puts Europe's push for digital sovereignty at the center of the launch.

In simple terms, that's about having more control over your technology and data, rather than relying on a few large suppliers.

I think supporters of that movement will welcome this approach. Running the management console on your own servers gives you more control over where management data and policies live. Using a separate browser engine also helps avoid depending on the same technology everywhere.

Firefox Mozilla

Credit: JHVEPhoto / Shutterstock

There’s growing talk of digital sovereignty as enterprises rethink past consolidation decisions made in the name of simplicity.

Mozilla, developer of Firefox, argues that a “very specific, very important layer” has been mostly missing from that conversation: The browser.

To that end, the company has unveiled Firefox Enterprise in a bid to diversify the browser engine to support privacy, control, and security.
